title: Run view — five layouts
brief: Five layouts for traj_compare's standalone RUN view — one target and all its runs (sim + 14 real repeats) — with a TensorBoard-style run list on the left, repeats as lines for a few and percentile bands for many, and the torque breakdown (target, commanded, feedforward, feedback, applied) first class.
invariants: Same SIMULATED fixture (fixture.py) and hero target: full-circle-slow, sim + 14 real repeats (8 × ff v1, 6 × ff v2).
1440 × 900 hero; traj_compare's own style.css, uPlot and three.js, loaded by <script src> from file://.
Fixed component colours: feedforward #3b82f6, feedback #f97316, target grey dashed, commanded = run colour, applied thin.
Degrees for angles, N·m for torque; FB share = Σ|fb| / (Σ|ff| + Σ|fb|); error = target − run.
Run colours keyed by config (sim grey, ff v1 violet, ff v2 green), never blue/orange; amber only for problems.
Every side panel drags (width remembered) and folds; time cursor and x zoom shared by every plot on the page.
boundary: Standalone front-end prototypes over the SIMULATED shared fixture (fixture.py); run/build.py re-grids each run onto its target's time grid and computes the per-run torque budget, the page computes bands over the runs you select. Not wired into traj_compare's report.py / plots.js; no real rig data.

requirements.name: Torque breakdown readable
requirements.why: Zach does not see the FF/FB split as first class today; it is the headline of this round (CONTRACT.md).
requirements.passCondition: For a joint and run: target, commanded, feedforward, feedback, applied; how much is feedback is evident.

anchors.5: the split reads at a glance and at any instant

requirements.name: Repeat distribution
requirements.why: real vs real × N: a few repeats as lines, many as median + percentile fans (TensorBoard histogram style).
requirements.passCondition: N repeats of the target as lines or percentile bands, automatic or switchable.

anchors.5: bands everywhere, lines on demand, one run highlightable against the band

requirements.name: Where / when
requirements.why: The bad moment has to be located in time and in the robot's pose, not just reported as an RMS.
requirements.passCondition: Error, torque and 3D share the time cursor and zoom, so the bad moment is located.

anchors.5: cursor + zoom + an explicit "worst moment" jump

requirements.name: Runs on the left
requirements.why: "Take a bit of the TensorBoard layout, with the runs on the left"; runs grouped by target.
requirements.passCondition: TensorBoard-like run list: toggle, solo, group by tag.

anchors.5: list with groups, solo, colour key, tag filter

requirements.name: Calm density
requirements.why: One calm answer first, detail on demand (Zach's UI rule); today's view opens on a wall of tables.
requirements.passCondition: Progressive disclosure, not a wall of 40 plots.

anchors.5: one calm answer, detail on demand

requirements.name: Fits traj_compare
requirements.why: The winner has to land in the existing stack, not as a rewrite.
requirements.passCondition: Buildable in the existing stack (vanilla JS, uPlot, three.js, sections, transport).

hardGates.name: Self-contained
hardGates.why: Standalone pages open from file:// with no server and no CDN (traj_compare's contract).

hardGates.name: Units
hardGates.why: Angles in degrees, tool in mm, torque in N·m; SI stays in the stored data.

hardGates.name: Honest data
hardGates.why: Everything shown comes from the shared fixture; every page says SIMULATED.

hardGates.name: Robot model
hardGates.why: A run view with 3D keeps the robot model available (skill contract).

variants.name: Sidebar + sections
variants.thesis: Today's run view, TensorBoard-ified: a run tree on the left and traj_compare's own section stack on the right, with a new Torque breakdown section; repeats collapse into percentile bands past five per group.
variants.bestWhen: You want the smallest step from today's viewer: same sections, same chips, same transport, now with runs on the left and the torque split as a section.
variants.losesWhen: You need error, torque and 3D on one screen — the 3D and error sections sit below the fold, so locating a moment means scrolling.

variants.name: Torque cockpit
variants.thesis: The torque is the page: per joint the command is drawn as what it is made of — feedforward as a blue area, feedback as the orange wedge between feedforward and commanded — one run at a time against its group's band, with the budget beside it.
variants.bestWhen: The question is "how much of the command is feedback, when, and is this run typical?" — the wedge thickness is the feedback at every instant.
variants.losesWhen: You want to see many runs' breakdowns at once, or signals other than torque and error; it is deliberately one run at a time.

variants.losesWhen: You want to cross-read two answers at once (torque split at the worst moment) — that means switching tabs.

variants.name: Joint × signal grid
variants.thesis: A spreadsheet of small multiples: rows are joints, columns are signals (error, commanded, feedforward, feedback, FB share, …), every cell carries each config's repeat band with the highlighted run on top; torque columns share one y scale per row so feedforward and feedback compare by size.
variants.bestWhen: Scanning for which joint × signal is off, across many repeats — every cell has the same encoding, so the eye compares cells, not legends.
variants.losesWhen: You need the composition at one instant (FF + FB = commanded) — the components live in separate cells.
